name: Optimize SQLite index creation and retrieval in pi-session-manager

description: Baseline harness crash: project_path filter query returned zero hits because the synthetic dataset only put 'tokio async' into sessions whose cwd did not match /workspace/project-b. Need to rebalance fixture text so every query shape has stable hits before measuring performance.

Baseline benchmark succeeded at 602.34ms, but checks failed for an unrelated existing feature-gating issue: CLI-only test invocation compiles `main-cli.rs`, which references `readonly::embedding*` APIs gated behind `gui`. Need to narrow checks to relevant search/migration tests under the normal feature set so correctness backpressure matches the code under study.

Baseline established with preserved benchmark harness (`autoresearch.sql_index_bench.rs`) and corrected checks. Median total time is 604.36ms across real init + indexing + mixed retrieval workload; ingest dominates at ~500.9ms, making session/message entry maintenance the most likely first optimization target.

Improved pre-parsed message entry upsert path by eliminating the duplicate `DELETE FROM message_entries` and reusing a cached insert statement. This directly targets ingest overhead in `upsert_session` and reduced median total time from 604.36ms to 570.69ms (~5.6%), almost entirely from ingest (500.9ms -> 469.4ms).

Discarded optimistic delete-only fast path in `delete_message_entries_for_session`. Removing the per-call table/schema probes looked promising, but median total time regressed to 582.00ms (vs best 570.69ms), with ingest rising back to 477.4ms. The branch probably benefited from SQLite’s existing happy-path behavior less than expected, so the extra recovery-oriented simplification is not a net win.
